advice: Proposal for a distinct experiment: pack A in K-major panels sized 32 rows by 32 K values. For each row block and K block, gather each source row’s contiguous K segment and write it into a compact panel so the outer-product loop can load A vectors contiguously for successive K steps. Adapt the SME consumer to traverse those panels, retaining the existing four ZA accumulators and FP32 FMOPA order. Keep temporary allocation and packing within gemm. Hypothesis: panel layout may reduce the amount of transpose work and improve A access during consumption. This is unverified; compare the complete timed call, including allocation, packing, and consumption, against the current path at n=512 and across supported small, odd, boundary, and large sizes. Preserve the general ABI and fallback behavior.
risks: This changes both packing and A consumption, so correctness and timing effects cannot be attributed to packing alone. Panel traversal may add address overhead or hurt cache behavior; setup cost may outweigh any consumption benefit, especially for small n. Check the fixed 0.002 tolerance, n<=0 no-op, odd and tile-boundary tails, and allocation-failure behavior. Use repeated paired controls under the fixed benchmark and power settings, and report spread. Do not infer speed from instruction counts or claim a gain without fresh measurements.
